task: Make Lattice CLI Authority runner flows accept host-neutral provider declarations instead of rejecting non-enum host names locally.
outcome: A senior developer can place the server-generated three-file bundle in a project, set LATTICE_AUTHORITY_RUNNER_PROVIDER=codex-cli, claude-code, antigravity, or another host declaration, then run Authority register/heartbeat/SSE/claim/takeover flows without a local unsupported-provider enum error; SSE jobs.available is only the streaming hint for the same POST claim/status contract, and if the server rejects the declaration, the terminal says it is a server policy or authorization rejection.
facts: The blocking local enum is normalizeAuthorityRunnerProvider in packages/main/src/core/authority-mode.ts.

buildAuthorityReadiness, buildAuthorityEnforceRunnerPlan, readLiveRunnerOptions, and buildLiveRunnerOptionsFromEnv consume runnerProviderValid and currently fail before the server can evaluate custom declarations.
authority_job_create also exposes a closed z.enum provider argument, which can block host-neutral queued job routing.
SSE jobs.available must stay aligned with POST signed claim/status semantics: it is a notification hint, not a separate ownership API.
Server-side provider authorization is already owned by Authority Server story B-e9cb.
SSE jobs.available is only a hint; signed claim remains the ownership boundary.
constraints: Do not add a hardcoded exhaustive host product enum.
Do not weaken API key, actor key, signature, lease, or server policy enforcement.
Do not rewrite scheduler or automatic host selection in this story.
Do not move server-owned senior bundle generation into the CLI.
Do not push to remote or use .omx.
